items.title: Claude plugins can auto-connect at login through MCP servers that accept Claude as a trusted issuer
items.summary: Claude can now connect a user's plugins automatically when they sign in, as long as the plugin's MCP server trusts Claude as a token issuer. Team and Enterprise admins set a plugin up once and teammates are connected on first use with no separate plugin login. Anthropic is asking plugin builders to add support for this.

doubt.pushback: One quote (@jatingargiitk) notes that tokens already issued do not vanish when an employee is removed, so offboarding still needs testing.

items.title: Simon Willison: Qwen 3.8 27B on a laptop also identifies games from raw policy-network weights
items.summary: Simon ran the no-tools prompts from the Weight-Space Programming paper, which give a model only the floating point weights of a small game-playing network, against Qwen 3.8 27B in LM Studio. It correctly named Pac-Man, Pong and Breakout after 46 to 65 minutes of reasoning each and failed on Freeway. He separates this no-tools reading from the paper's tool-using weight edits and says the wider hype is not justified.

items.title: Allen AI StateBench: frontier models drop to 13% or lower on long state-tracking problems
items.summary: StateBench is a new eval for following state changes across long text, like an object changing hands or a variable being reassigned. Ai2 reports that GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 fall to 13% accuracy or lower on the hardest, longest problems. Code and data are on GitHub.

items.title: E2B Workload Identity gives every sandbox a signed identity instead of long-lived credentials
items.summary: Each E2B sandbox now carries a signed identity, so a backend can tell which sandbox is calling and decide what it may access without handing out and rotating long-lived secrets. Generally available on E2B Cloud and supported in bring-your-own-cloud.

items.title: Perplexity pplx-embed-v2-context: open-weight 9B and 0.6B contextual embedding models, tuned with turbopuffer
items.summary: Perplexity released open-weight vision-language embedding models at 9B and 0.6B that return one int8 vector per document, or one per chunk where each chunk's vector is computed with the whole document in view. turbopuffer says it evaluated Perplexity's checkpoints against its private retrieval benchmark during training, and a joint paper is on arXiv.

items.title: LeRobot adds Galaxea G0.5, a 2B vision-language-action model that plans subtasks and boxes before acting
items.summary: G0.5 is an open 2B VLA built on Qwen3.5. Before each chunk of actions it predicts the current subtask, bounding boxes for the objects involved, and then the actions conditioned on that reasoning. LeRobot's annotation pipeline can also generate plans, memory and visual Q&A for datasets.

items.title: Gemini API CLI now ships as an agent skill
items.summary: Google packaged the Gemini API CLI (kept 2026-10-26) as an installable skill so a coding agent can call Gemini for images, speech, video and files without one-off scripts. Install is npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --skill gemini-api-cli.

items.title: Cua Driver works with Google Antigravity's agent across desktop apps
items.summary: A new Google AI Studio integration guide lets the Antigravity agent drive apps on your computer, with each task in its own background Cua Driver session, on macOS, Windows and Linux. Relevant because Antigravity (agy) is in the fleet.

items.title: LlamaIndex makes OCRia-1 generate tokens nearly 10x faster on one B200
items.summary: LlamaIndex's infra team stacked seventeen small serving optimizations, each checked for speed and accuracy, to get its OCRia-1 document parsing model close to 10x faster token generation on a single B200. They wrote up the method and plan to upstream some changes to vLLM.

items.title: OpenRouter Guardrails add org-wide policies with per-person budget and model exceptions
items.summary: Admins can now set budget, model access and moderation rules for a whole org, then give specific people bigger budgets or more models inside those limits, and change each policy on its own.

items.title: Prime Intellect finds and fixes issues in popular public evals
items.summary: Prime Intellect audited several widely used public evaluations, found problems, fixed them and published its findings. The post does not name the evals; details are in the linked write-up.

items.title: safeagents judge bench tests whether a judge model can spot agent tool-call misbehavior
items.summary: A new Hugging Face dataset checks if a decision model can flag bad agent tool calls such as reward hacking, sandbox escape and harness introspection.

items.title: colibri: pure C runtime that runs 744B MoE models in about 10GB of RAM by tiering experts
items.summary: colibri keeps hot MoE experts on the GPU, warm ones in RAM and cold ones on NVMe, so very large MoE models like GLM-5.2, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash can run on a normal PC behind a local OpenAI-compatible API. The numbers come from an aggregator post, not the author, and speed is not stated.

doubt.pushback: Second-hand post with no throughput figures; expect very slow generation from NVMe.
